nfr_classifications.title: Digital claim submission

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Claim submission must be tied to an authenticated employee identity — no anonymous submissions
Employee must receive an explicit on-screen confirmation the claim was submitted, since there is no paper or email trail as evidence
Claim submission response time — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Security and usability boundaries follow directly from the statement's own terms ('employee', 'digitally, without paper or email'); no response-time figure is stated anywhere in requirements.md, vision.md, or regulatory-feasibility.md, so Performance is marked TBD rather than guessed.

nfr_classifications.title: Single approver dashboard

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Approver must see every pending claim in a single view, not split across pages or tabs requiring reconstruction
Expected concurrent pending-claim volume per approver — TBD — needs stakeholder input
Dashboard uptime target — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: 'One dashboard view' directly implies the usability boundary; no volume or uptime figure is stated anywhere in the input, and this internal tool has no enterprise-security KB entry (that KB covers a different fictional organisation), so both are marked TBD rather than assumed from a generic SLA.

nfr_classifications.title: Submission-to-payment time reporting

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Submission-to-payment elapsed time under 5 business days
Elapsed-time records must be tied to the originating claim and employee, not aggregated anonymously

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Performance directly restates the FR's own explicit 5-business-day target; Security follows from the FR's own per-claim, per-employee tracking requirement.

content.execution_summary:
• Classified 3 functional requirements (FR-001–FR-003) against kb-L1-nfr-classification-taxonomy's six categories.
• Categories applied: Security x2, Usability x2, Performance x2, Scalability x1, Availability x1 — none padded to a fixed six.
• 3 boundary conditions left genuinely TBD (submission response time, pending-claim volume, dashboard uptime) — no explicit or implied figure found in requirements.md/vision.md/regulatory-feasibility.md.
• Key decision: did not cite kb-L1-enterprise-security for this scenario — that KB's content is scoped to a different fictional parent enterprise (Thornbury Foods Group) and does not apply to this internal tool's own organisation.
• Reflection: every non-TBD condition cites a specific source, every TBD condition has source '—', ids match requirements.md exactly.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-nfr-classification-taxonomy (category questions/forms for all 3 FRs); kb-L1-enterprise-architecture, kb-L1-enterprise-security (checked, not applicable to this scenario).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-output-schema-validator (pass), gr-L1-consistency-check (pass).
• Gaps flagged: 3 TBDs need stakeholder input before design (submission latency, dashboard concurrency, dashboard uptime).
